Rarefaction of a statistic over sampling effort

Source: R/sampling.R
trait_rarefaction.Rd

Computes a statistic of the individuals, such as the mean T-statistics of tstats() or the decomposition of trait_flex(), on repeated subsamples of decreasing effort, with the schemes of subsample_individuals(). By default effort is the number of individuals per population: n individuals are drawn from each population (populations smaller than n keep all their individuals), for a series of n. With cover, effort is instead the share of the abundance of each site covered by the species measured, from the most abundant down; all individuals of those species are kept, or n of them when a single n is given. The curve shows how much effort is needed before the statistic stops changing. This rarefies individuals within populations or species within sites; the rarefaction of species richness (for instance vegan::rarefy() or the package iNEXT) answers another question.

Usage

trait_rarefaction(
  individuals,
  statistic = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  cover = NULL,
  reps = 20,
  level = 0.95,
  min_n = 2,
  site = "site",
  species = "species",
  abundance = NULL
)

Arguments

individuals

Data frame with one row per individual.

statistic

Function of a data frame of individuals that returns a named numeric vector. The default gives the mean over sites of the three T-statistics of tstats() for the column trait.

n

Numbers of individuals per population; the default runs from 2 to the median size of the populations. With cover, a single number of individuals per population, or NULL (the default) to keep all of them.

cover

Shares (0 to 1) of abundance covered by the species measured, for a rarefaction over species instead of individuals; NULL (the default) for a rarefaction over n.

reps

Number of subsamples for each level of effort. With cover and no n the subsamples are all equal, and a single one is computed.

level

Coverage of the interval of the statistic over subsamples.

min_n, site, species

Passed to subsample_individuals(). With min_n = 2 (the default) populations of one individual are left out, as in tstats() analyses.

abundance

Name of a column with the abundance of each population, used with cover (passed to subsample_individuals()).

Value

A data frame of class trait_rarefaction with the columns effort (n or cover, as the attribute by says), statistic (the names returned by statistic), mean, low and high (quantiles over subsamples) and reps (subsamples with a finite value), with a plot() method. The values of all subsamples are in the attribute values.

See also

subsample_individuals(), tstats().

Other trait variation among individuals: community_index(), neighbour_metrics, nested_variance(), null_intervals(), plot.mc_trait_gradient(), plot.nested_variance(), plot.trait_flex(), plot.trait_rarefaction(), plot.tstats(), plot_population_traits(), population_shifts(), sample_individuals(), subsample_individuals(), trait_densities(), trait_flex(), trait_gradient(), trait_gradient_bayes(), trait_gradient_phylo(), trait_gradient_test(), trait_gradient_weights(), tstats(), tstats_summary()

Examples

set.seed(1)
ind <- data.frame(site = rep(paste0("s", 1:5), each = 40),
                  species = sample(c("a", "b", "c"), 200, replace = TRUE))
ind$trait <- c(a = 10, b = 12, c = 15)[ind$species] + rnorm(200)
rare <- trait_rarefaction(ind, n = c(2, 4, 8), reps = 10)
rare
#>   effort statistic      mean       low      high reps
#> 1      2   T_IP.IC 0.1792578 0.1114679 0.2825401   10
#> 2      2   T_IC.IR 1.1253155 1.0673701 1.1558713   10
#> 3      2   T_PC.PR 1.3538095 1.2787934 1.3944207   10
#> 4      4   T_IP.IC 0.1761934 0.1233734 0.2363405   10
#> 5      4   T_IC.IR 1.0593501 1.0317182 1.0713293   10
#> 6      4   T_PC.PR 1.3799166 1.3390941 1.3978650   10
#> 7      8   T_IP.IC 0.1863448 0.1504747 0.2177141   10
#> 8      8   T_IC.IR 1.0330574 1.0312667 1.0339801   10
#> 9      8   T_PC.PR 1.3972044 1.3943099 1.3987061   10
# over the share of abundance covered by the species measured
trait_rarefaction(ind, cover = c(0.5, 0.8, 1))
#>   effort statistic      mean       low      high reps
#> 1    0.5   T_IP.IC 0.3638244 0.3638244 0.3638244    1
#> 2    0.5   T_IC.IR 0.7635113 0.7635113 0.7635113    1
#> 3    0.5   T_PC.PR 1.2750472 1.2750472 1.2750472    1
#> 4    0.8   T_IP.IC 0.1958225 0.1958225 0.1958225    1
#> 5    0.8   T_IC.IR 1.0114336 1.0114336 1.0114336    1
#> 6    0.8   T_PC.PR 1.3996447 1.3996447 1.3996447    1
#> 7    1.0   T_IP.IC 0.1958225 0.1958225 0.1958225    1
#> 8    1.0   T_IC.IR 1.0114336 1.0114336 1.0114336    1
#> 9    1.0   T_PC.PR 1.3996447 1.3996447 1.3996447    1
